newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says five groups plan northeast railway bid.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says five groups plan northeast railway bid.

text.p: Five companies have registered to bid for rights to operate Mexico's northeast railroad line, the communications and transportation ministry said Tuesday in Diario Official, the government gazette.
One of the prospective bidding groups is Mexican constructor Empresas ICA Sociedad Controladora in association with U.S. companies Union Pacific Railroad Company and SCB International Railways LLC.
Another expected bidder is Consorcio Ferrocarril Centro Mexico, an alliance linking Mexican businessman Carlos Abedrop Davila, GEC Alsthom Transport and French Systra-Sofretu-Sofrerail.

Three separate bids came from mining company Grupo Mexico, U.S.-based Illinois Central Corp and Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana, an alliance of transport company Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and U.S.-based Kansas City Southern Industries.

Bids to operate the railway are due November 29, and a decision is expected by December 16, the government said. The northeast railroad is the second scheduled for auction as part of Mexico's railroad privatization program.

The northeast railroad includes routes connecting Mexico City and Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas state; Monterrey, Nuevo Leon state and Matamoros, Tamaulipas; Aguascalientes, Aguascalientes state and Tampico, Tamaulipas; Mexico City and Veracruz, Veracruz state and Mexico City and Lazaro Cardenas, Michocan state.
